modelResponse.episodeSummary: Helen M. Kowalski, 72F, Junctional Escape Rhythm, critical, hypotensive
keyECGEvidence: preEventNote: ECG changes are disproportionately mild relative to potassium level; bradycardia severity exceeds what K+ 6.4 alone would typically produce; atropine 1 mg x2 administered with no heart rate response
modelResponse.mechanism: Hyperkalemia-induced conduction block (AV block) leading to escape rhythm
contributingFactors: Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) on Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD)

rejectedAlternatives.why: Patient has no prior arrhythmia history. The severe hyperkalemia (K 6.4 mmol/L HIGH) and AKI (Cr 3.2 mg/dL CRITICAL HIGH) are more likely causes of bradycardia and AV block than new-onset intrinsic conduction disease.

While atenolol can cause bradycardia, the severity (rate 32 bpm) and lack of response to atropine, coupled with the critical hyperkalemia and AKI, point towards a more acute and severe underlying cause. The ECG morphology is also consistent with a junctional escape rather than just sinus bradycardia.
No data available to support hypothyroidism. The acute presentation with severe hyperkalemia and AKI is a more direct explanation.

recommendedActions: Administer Calcium Gluconate 1g IV push immediately
Administer Insulin 10 units IV with 50 mL D50W
Administer Sodium Bicarbonate 100 mEq IV push (if acidosis is severe, consider continuous infusion)
Administer Albuterol nebulized (e.g., 2.5 mg in 2.5 mL NS)
Consider transcutaneous pacing if hemodynamically unstable and unresponsive to medical management
uncertainty: Exact cause of AKI (pre-renal vs. intrinsic) is unclear but likely multifactorial.
No information on baseline renal function beyond CKD stage 3.
No information on current medications other than home meds and NS bolus.
